page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v6 is a high-vCPU virtual machine designed for compute-intensive workloads that require lower memory density than standard cloud configurations. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and modern instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512. The system provides 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64ls_v6 delivers strong multi-threaded computational performance, achieving top-decile results in Geekbench multi-core processing, image manipulation, and static web serving throughput at 100.53 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests reveal cached small-block read speeds reaching 4604.62 GB/sec alongside uncached large-block reads of 258.84 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates solid execution across Clang software compilation, PassMark encryption routines, Redis operations reaching 84.81 million SET operations per second, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.

A key architectural consideration of the D64ls_v6 is the absence of local disk storage and discrete GPU accelerators, requiring all persistent storage to be handled over the network. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation minimizes unused memory overhead, offering favorable compute density for CPU-bound tasks. This profile makes the instance well suited for continuous integration build systems, large web-serving farms, distributed caching nodes, batch transformation pipelines, and parallel compute workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v6 is a compute-focused instance within the Dlsv6 series, configured with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 128 GB of RAM, representing a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It features hardware extensions including Intel AMX and AVX-512, contributing to top-tier multi-core Geekbench and static web serving throughput results. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs, relying on remote block storage for persistent data. This hardware profile provides resource efficiency for CPU-bound tasks where large per-core memory footprints are unnecessary. D64ls_v6 is suited for large-scale web serving, Clang software compilation, Redis caching tiers, batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
